evidence_chain.finding: At identical 5/2.5/2.5-cm lower-boundary support, D8_B2P5 and D12_B2P5 groundwater responses are numerically indistinguishable; adding four distributed storage states does not rescue fidelity.
evidence_chain.implication: The remaining error is strongly tied to propagation/subgrid structure rather than missing broad storage totals.

evidence_chain.finding: A zero-fit constant-flux Darcian steady-equivalent closure fails its preregistered numerical admissibility route.
evidence_chain.implication: Quasi-steady two-point propagation does not provide an admissible next closure under its frozen contract.

evidence_chain.finding: Layer-integrated storage alone supplies only one integral constraint and does not uniquely determine transient subgrid tendency/profile shape.
evidence_chain.implication: Any storage-only transient reconstruction needs an additional scientific ansatz.

evidence_chain.finding: The most conservative storage-only ansatz, P0 uniform storage tendency, has conditional local uniqueness but fails prospective existence/admissibility over the frozen B14 domain: 264/405 local cases and 28/28 column cases fail.
evidence_chain.implication: The minimal conservation-aligned algebraic ansatz cannot proceed to hydrological response and is not retuned.

QUADRATIC_PRESSURE_PROFILE.structural_assumption: Choose a quadratic profile in native suction/pressure head, adding one algebraic shape mode per layer.
merits: Minimum polynomial degree that closes the C5V finite-dimensional degree count.
Uses the native hydraulic variable appearing in Darcy gradients and prescribed-head boundary conditions.
Can be made zero-fit and storage-consistent.
unresolved: No conservation principle uniquely selects pressure/suction rather than theta, hydraulic head or a transformed potential as the polynomial coordinate.
Profile order remains a structural modeling choice.
Selecting this family now would be a new ansatz choice rather than a consequence of existing state authority.

TRANSFORMED_POTENTIAL_PROFILE.structural_assumption: Choose a low-order profile in a constitutive transform such as a Kirchhoff hydraulic potential.
merits: Kirchhoff transforms are established tools for reducing nonlinear conductivity structure in Richards numerics.
The transformed coordinate is physically tied to the conductivity integral.
unresolved: For general van Genuchten-Mualem relations the transform does not uniquely remove all transient/gravity nonlinearity.
Transform definition and profile order remain scientific choices not determined by layer storage.
Its constitutive-integral structure is adjacent to, though not identical with, the DSE2P route that already encountered admissibility problems.

literature_due_diligence.conclusion: Mass-conservative mixed Richards formulations privilege correct storage/time treatment, but do not select a unique within-control-volume hydraulic profile.
Finite-volume state variables are naturally cell averages and P0 is the lowest-order projection; higher-order reconstruction requires additional structural information.

literature_due_diligence.reference: Suk & Park (2019), Journal of Hydrology 579:124213, doi:10.1016/j.jhydrol.2019.124213
literature_due_diligence.conclusion: Kirchhoff transformation is a useful Richards numerical coordinate, but its benefits depend on constitutive structure and it does not establish a unique reduced subgrid profile.
Quadratic vertical profiles are used as low-parameter empirical reconstructions when observations are limited; that supports feasibility, not physical uniqueness.

literature_due_diligence.reference: Bootsma, van der Ploeg & Weerts (2026), Advances in Water Resources 213:105327, doi:10.1016/j.advwatres.2026.105327
literature_due_diligence.conclusion: A DAE view retaining moisture content with pressure linked by constitutive constraint reinforces the distinction between conserved moisture state and hydraulic algebraic variables; it does not remove the need for unresolved spatial information in an aggregated layer.

constraints: Theory/degree-count/conservation derivation only before any response experiment.
